summary: The shared monoidal and presentable enhancement, animation and its two comparison returns. The existing targets are retained and refined; additional targets supply Verdier quotients, monoidal localization, descendability, dualizability without compact generation, rigid categories and formal inversion. Stability, sheaf enhancement, adjoints, cotangent complexes and concrete spectra are imported from their owners. All six stages are planned, with explicit remaining obligations and no implementation claims.

nodes.title: Symmetric monoidal infinity-categories
nodes.statement: A symmetric monoidal infinity-category is a cocartesian fibration C⊗ → N(Fin_*) whose fibre over ⟨n⟩ maps equivalently to C^n through the n inert projections; C is the fibre at ⟨1⟩. The fibre at ⟨0⟩ is terminal. Active fold maps give tensor products and the nullary fold gives the unit.
hypotheses: Work in specified nested universes; finite pointed sets are ordinary finite sets with a distinguished base point.
Cocartesian lifts over all maps are required, not only inert lifts.
proofSteps: Extend E0’s restricted straightening to the base N(Fin_*); assemble the fibrewise product diagrams.
Impose the Segal equivalences and recover coherent tensor and unit from active lifts.

Construct the ordinary operadic category from finite lists and multimorphisms, using the associator and symmetry coherence of the ordinary category, and compare its nerve fibrewise. The pinned Grothendieck construction applies to a strict category-valued diagram; use it only after such a strict diagram or strictification has been supplied.
acceptance: The zero-ary fibre is equivalent to the terminal infinity-category.
The one-ary fibre is equivalent to the underlying category.
For an ordinary symmetric monoidal C the homotopy category of the underlying fibre is equivalent to C.

nodes.title: Infinity-operads
nodes.statement: An infinity-operad O⊗ → N(Fin_*) is an inner fibration with cocartesian inert lifts. For each map f:⟨m⟩→⟨n⟩, its mapping space over f is the product of the mapping spaces over ρ_i f to the n output colours. Its fibre at ⟨n⟩ is equivalent, via inert projections, to the n-fold product of its colour fibre. The mapping-space condition includes nullary operations.

An infinity-operad need not admit active cocartesian lifts.
proofSteps: Construct the inert/active factorization in Fin_*.
Use E0 mapping spaces and lifting predicates to state the inert, operation-product and object-Segal axioms.
Check the commutative operad and the associative operad with ordered fibres.
acceptance: The colour category of the commutative operad is terminal.
The associative n-input operation space has n! components, represented by total orders.
The associative zero-input operation space is terminal.

nodes.title: Monoidal categories over an operad
nodes.statement: An O-monoidal infinity-category is a cocartesian fibration C⊗ → O⊗ such that, for T with inert components T_i, C_T → ∏_i C_(T_i) is an equivalence. The composite to N(Fin_*) is then an infinity-operad. A map is O-monoidal if it preserves cocartesian edges; it is lax O-monoidal if it is an operad map and only preserves the inert edges.
hypotheses: O⊗ is an infinity-operad.
The product condition is on the fibres over individual objects T of O⊗.
proofSteps: Use the fibre criterion in HA 2.1.2.12, rather than assuming any cocartesian fibration is monoidal.
Compose the operadic maps and verify the mapping-space and Segal conditions.
Build the full functor categories of strong and lax maps over the base.
acceptance: For O=Comm, this recovers symmetric monoidal categories.
The identity operad map is strong monoidal.
A lax map supplies a unit comparison; a strong map has an invertible unit comparison.

nodes.title: Operadic algebras
nodes.statement: Alg_O(C) is the full infinity-category of sections O⊗ → C⊗ over O⊗ that preserve inert edges. For O=Comm write CAlg(C); for O=Ass use associative algebra objects. Algebra maps are coherent transformations over the operad. In a cartesian monoidal ordinary category, the construction agrees with ordinary commutative or associative monoid objects after passing to nerves.
hypotheses: C⊗ is O-monoidal.
A section need not preserve active cocartesian edges.
proofSteps: Form the functor category over O⊗ using E0; select inert-preserving sections.
Compare with ordinary algebra objects by evaluating operation maps.

Compose an associative algebra section with the cuts functor Δop→Ass⊗ to obtain a diagram in the total operadic category, whose n-th value is the n-tuple of its underlying object. For cartesian tensor this corresponds to a Segal simplicial object in the underlying category, with A_n≃A_1^n and A_0 terminal; the product-valued description is not asserted for a general tensor.
acceptance: Algebras in the terminal monoidal category form a terminal category.

nodes.title: Modules and extension of scalars
nodes.statement: For an associative algebra A in C and a left C-tensored infinity-category M, LMod_A(M) is the fibre of the category of LM-algebras at A. Its objects have a coherently unital associative action A⊗M→M. If C and M admit geometric realizations, and both the tensor in C and its action on M preserve them separately in each variable, f:A→B has an extension-of-scalars left adjoint B⊗_A− to restriction. Compute it by the two-sided bar realization.
hypotheses: LM is the two-coloured operad distinguishing the algebra and module colours.
For a commutative A in presentably symmetric monoidal C, Mod_A(C) has relative tensor and unit A; tensors must preserve colimits.
proofSteps: Apply the algebra-section construction to LM and take the fibre over A.
Realize Bar(B,A,M) and prove its mapping-space adjunction with restriction.
Use commutativity of A to descend tensor and its symmetry to the relative bar construction.
acceptance: Modules over the tensor unit are equivalent to C.

nodes.title: Stable monoidal enhancement comparison
nodes.statement: Import E0’s stable infinity-category and its exact/triangulated API. If C is also symmetric monoidal and its tensor is exact separately, the tensor descends to a symmetric monoidal structure on hC compatible with suspension and distinguished cofiber triangles. For derived modules it agrees with Mathlib’s ordinary derived category through E1’s enhancement; constructing the tensor uses K-flat replacements, not closure of K-injectives under tensor.

Require exactness separately; it does not follow from merely having a monoidal structure.
proofSteps: Transport the operadic coherent tensor along h and identify its associator, unit and symmetry.
Apply E0’s finite cofiber/triangle comparison to tensor in either variable.
Use E1’s derived tensor comparison to ordinary complexes.
acceptance: For R-modules, the monoidal homotopy-category comparison sends the enhanced tensor unit to R[0] and a cofiber triangle to the pinned cochain cone triangle.
Tensoring the triangle R→R→0 by any K gives K→K→0, with the E0 shift convention.

nodes.title: Exact monoidal functors and triangles
nodes.statement: For stable C,D, import E0’s equivalence of finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation. An exact strong or lax monoidal functor then induces the corresponding ordinary monoidal functor on homotopy categories and carries the cofiber triangle of f to that of Ff, with the suspension comparison inherited from E0. Coherent functors are retained before passing to homotopy categories.
hypotheses: Exactness is an E0 property of the underlying functor.
Lax monoidal does not imply exact, and exact does not imply strong monoidal.
proofSteps: Restrict the coherent strong/lax functor categories by E0 exactness.
Apply h, transport suspension isomorphisms, and verify compatibility with the tensor structure.
acceptance: The suspension comparison for the identity functor is the identity; comparisons compose naturally for two exact monoidal functors.
For extension of scalars R→S, the image of a cone triangle is the derived-tensor cone triangle, without a flatness assumption on S.

nodes.title: Idempotent completion and its monoidal extension
nodes.statement: Idem(C) is the full subcategory of P(C) spanned by retracts of representables. C→Idem(C) is fully faithful; restriction Fun(Idem(C),D)→Fun(C,D) is an equivalence for idempotent-complete D. For small stable C it is stable. A separately exact tensor extends to retracts, giving a symmetric monoidal completion and the corresponding monoidal universal property. For an ordinary category C this agrees with the nerve of its Mathlib Karoubi envelope.
hypotheses: Use homotopy coherent idempotents, not just idempotents in hC.
The ordinary comparison has discrete mapping spaces; no claim hIdem(C)=Karoubi(hC) in complete generality is needed.
proofSteps: Take the retract closure of the representable Yoneda image in space-valued presheaves.
Use HTT’s functor restriction theorem for uniqueness of extensions.
Extend tensor on retracts and check closure of finite cofibers using E0.
acceptance: Completing a completed category changes it by an equivalence.
Idem(NC) is equivalent to N(Karoubi C).
Idem(*) is terminal.

nodes.title: Symmetric monoidal Dwyer–Kan localization
nodes.statement: If C⊗ is symmetric monoidal and a class W of underlying morphisms is stable under tensoring with any object in either variable, C[W⁻¹] carries a symmetric monoidal structure. The localization is strong monoidal. Restriction is fully faithful on strong and on lax monoidal functor categories with essential image the functors inverting W. For every base change K→N(Fin_*), the total operadic localization is the corresponding Dwyer–Kan localization.
hypotheses: Use the saturated class generated by W; an ordinary categorical localization of hC alone does not supply this theorem.
The tensor-stability hypothesis is essential for the fibrewise assertion.
proofSteps: Mark the vertical product edges of W in the fibres of C⊗.
Localize the total space over Fin_* and use inert/product compatibility to prove the Segal equivalences.
Verify universal properties after arbitrary base change; distinguish the strong and lax subcategories.
acceptance: Localizing only equivalences recovers C and its unit.
Restriction on both strong and lax functor categories is fully faithful and its essential image inverts each specified W-map; check inert as well as nullary operations.
For any K→N(Fin_*), the operadic localization comparison after pullback is an equivalence.

nodes.title: Monoidal localization of a model category
nodes.statement: A symmetric monoidal model category satisfying the pushout-product and unit axioms has a symmetric monoidal infinity-localization. The localization of cofibrant objects computes the derived tensor and is strongly monoidally equivalent to the underlying Dwyer–Kan localization with this derived structure. The map from the category of all objects is lax monoidal and initial among lax monoidal functors inverting weak equivalences. This operadic localization is compatible with base change over Fin_*. If the original unit is not cofibrant, the derived unit is represented by its cofibrant replacement; no strong all-object localization map is asserted.
hypotheses: The model structure and Quillen tensor hypotheses must be supplied for each application.
Tensor need not preserve weak equivalences between all objects; cofibrant replacements are indispensable.
proofSteps: Apply tensor-compatible localization to cofibrant objects; the pushout-product axiom and Ken Brown argument give weak-equivalence preservation there. A cofibrant replacement of the unit supplies the derived nullary operation.
Use the unit axiom and cofibrant replacement to identify the all-object localization.
Construct the lax all-object comparison and verify its universal property on each fibre.
acceptance: For chain complexes, tensor on cofibrant replacements computes derived tensor; ordinary tensor on arbitrary nonflat complexes cannot replace it.
With a noncofibrant unit, its replacement still maps to the derived tensor unit.
The all-object localization supplies lax tensor and unit maps; an unsupported strong all-object comparison fails the specification.

nodes.title: Derived cocartesian families
nodes.statement: For a cocartesian fibration X→S over a small infinity-category, with vertical marked weak equivalences, call it left derivable when every transition has an absolute left derived functor, described as an absolute right Kan extension along the source localization, and the derived-composition comparisons are equivalences for all 2-simplices. Localizing X fibrewise gives a cocartesian fibration over S, with those derived transitions, compatible with base change by any small infinity-category K→S. The localization preserves original cocartesian lifts over a transition that preserves the marked weak equivalences; this is a sufficient condition, not a necessity assertion.
hypotheses: Left derived is the source-localization right-Kan convention of NS A.8.
S and every base-change K are small infinity-categories. E0 supplies restricted diagram shapes; the present construction requires the Cat∞ gluing argument for general S.
proofSteps: Extend restricted straightening by NS A.16–A.17: points and intervals generate Cat∞ under colimits, cocartesian families glue along those categorical colimits, and pullback preserves the gluing. A strict colimit of raw simplicial sets is not substituted for that colimit.
Localize fibres and derive transitions using E3 Kan extensions.
Use the absolute property and the 2-simplex comparisons to assemble a coherent functor S→Cat∞.
Apply NS A.14–A.15 to identify the total localization and its base-change comparison.
acceptance: Over a point the construction is the fibre localization.
Over Δ¹ the transition is the derived transition, not the underived functor.
For identity weak-equivalence classes the localized family is equivalent to the original one.

nodes.title: Stable subcategories and tensor ideals
nodes.statement: A stable subcategory D⊆C is a full subcategory closed under zero objects, fibers and cofibers; it need not be closed under retracts. In a stable monoidal C with separately exact tensor, it is a tensor ideal if X⊗Y lies in D whenever X lies in C and Y lies in D. The thick tensor ideal adds closure under retracts. For commutative A→B, the thick tensor ideal generated by B is taken in Mod_A(C), not in C unless A is the unit.

Keep stable, thick and localizing closure distinct.

Define the closures by intersection and derive inclusions and induction principles.
Tensor ideals and thick closure are used in quotient kernels and descendability.

nodes.title: Verdier quotient of a small stable infinity-category
nodes.statement: For small stable C and full stable D⊆C, C/D is the Dwyer–Kan localization at maps with cofiber in D. It is stable and universal for exact functors C→E annihilating D. For X,Y∈C its mapping space is the filtered colimit over maps Z→Y with Z∈D of Map_C(X,cofib(Z→Y)). The kernel on objects is the retract closure of D, rather than D itself when D is not thick. If D is a tensor ideal and tensor is separately exact, the quotient is symmetric monoidal with the analogous universal property for exact lax monoidal functors.
hypotheses: No compact-generation assumption is used.
Idempotent completion of the quotient is a separate construction.
proofSteps: Invert maps with cofiber in D; identify their calculus through the filtered approximation of Y by cofibers of Z→Y.
Use the formula to establish mapping-space universality and stability.
Apply monoidal localization to an ideal; derive the lax monoidal universality, preserving the distinction from strong maps.
acceptance: C/0 is equivalent to C.
C/C is the zero stable category.
q(ΣX) ≃ ΣqX.

nodes.title: Barr–Beck–Lurie monadicity
nodes.statement: For F:C⇄D:G with unit and counit, let T=GF be the coherent monad on C. The comparison D→LMod_T(C) is an equivalence precisely when G is conservative and D admits geometric realizations of G-split simplicial objects which G preserves. Split refers to the augmented simplicial diagram after applying G. The algebra comparison preserves the forgetful functor to C.
hypotheses: The coherent adjunction is imported from E3.
Preservation of all colimits is sufficient in applications but is not the criterion’s hypothesis.
proofSteps: Construct the coherent monad and comparison from the unit and counit.
Use the split augmented bar resolution and conservativity to prove full faithfulness and essential surjectivity.
Apply the exact G-split realization condition; do not replace it by unqualified preservation of arbitrary limits.
acceptance: For the free/forgetful adjunction on modules, the monadic comparison commutes with the forgetful functor.
For the identity adjunction, the monad is the identity and its module category recovers C.
Use G-split realizations and conservativity separately; neither condition can be discarded in the comparison.

nodes.title: Descendable algebras and finite index
nodes.statement: In a presentable stable symmetric monoidal C whose tensor preserves colimits separately, A→B is descendable when A belongs to the thick tensor ideal generated by B in Mod_A(C). Write I=fib(A→B). It has index at most m when the natural map I^⊗_A m→A is nullhomotopic. Descendability is equivalent to such a finite m and to the augmented Amitsur totalization tower being pro-isomorphic to the constant A tower. Its definition uses finite thick generation, not merely recovery of the completed unit by the infinite totalization.
hypotheses: m is a nonnegative integer; m=0 forces the unit A to be zero.
Nullhomotopy is a nullhomotopy of the map, stronger than vanishing on cohomology.
proofSteps: Define the augmentation fibre and its tensor powers in Mod_A(C).
Relate the cubical bar tower to the cosimplicial partial-totalization tower by a pro-comparison.
Use nilpotence of the augmentation maps to prove finite-index ⇔ thick generation ⇔ pro-constant Amitsur tower.
acceptance: An identity algebra map has index at most one.
Index at most zero forces A=0.
ℤ_p→𝔽_p is not descendable, although its Amitsur completion recovers the p-complete unit.

sources.match: Defines finite tensor nilpotence, characterizes it by thick generation and compares it with the pro-constant Amitsur tower.

nodes.title: Module descent and permanence of descendability
nodes.statement: For descendable A→B, Mod_A(C) → lim_[n] Mod_(B^⊗_A(n+1))(C) is a symmetric monoidal equivalence along extension-of-scalars transitions. Descendability is preserved by composition, by passage to an intermediate algebra, and by exact strong monoidal functors. Cocontinuous lax monoidal functors preserve a specified finite index after applying their algebra and module structure maps. For a finite simplicial diagram of presentably stable symmetric monoidal categories, a commutative algebra in its limit is descendable if and only if its evaluations at every vertex are descendable. Extension of scalars along a descendable map is conservative.
hypotheses: All limits of module categories are coherent limits.
For the finite-limit statement use a finite simplicial indexing set; arbitrary inverse limits are not asserted.
proofSteps: Use the finite index to show the augmented Amitsur resolutions are effective for every module.

Apply the dual Barr–Beck–Lurie criterion to extension of scalars, whose conservativity follows from finite thick generation; the finite-index Amitsur resolution supplies the required split-totalization preservation.

Transport the canonical augmentation-power nullhomotopy under the functor. For finite limits of categories use the pointwise detection of a pro-constant bar tower (Mathew Proposition 3.25); for conservativity use the thick-generation argument.

nodes.title: Uniform index and categorical descendability examples
nodes.statement: Fix a presentably stable symmetric monoidal category C and A∈CAlg(C), with tensor preserving colimits separately. Let I be a small filtered ordinary category such that derived inverse limits of Iᵒᵖ-diagrams of spectra have finite cohomological dimension. A coherent diagram of A-algebras B_i with every A→B_i of descendability index at most the same m has descendable colimit map A→colim_i B_i. For I=ℕ, index at most 2m suffices. Without a uniform bound this can fail. For ordinary rings, nilpotent ideal quotients are descendable, while a locally nilpotent ideal quotient need not be. A faithfully flat map with countably presented target algebra is descendable. If its source is Noetherian Gorenstein of Krull dimension d, a faithfully flat target has index at most d+1.
hypotheses: The source algebra A is fixed throughout the diagram. The finite cohomological dimension is a condition on derived limits of spectra over Iᵒᵖ, and the index bound is uniform in i.
Countably presented means both generators and relations, not merely countably generated.
For I=ℕ the BS proof gives a bound 2m through the vanishing of lim²; no quantitative bound for arbitrary I is asserted here.
proofSteps: For sequential diagrams apply the multiplicative derived-limit filtration to the powers of the augmentation map; two filtration-one maps have zero composite.
For finite-cohomological-dimension I use the finite derived-limit filtration and multiplicativity; isolate this general tower input in the recorded gap.
Apply the augmentation-fibre nilpotence criterion to nilpotent quotients and BS’s locally-nilpotent counterexample.
Import E1’s ordinary Ext/projective-dimension statements to obtain the Gorenstein bound; use Mathew Corollary 3.33 for countable presentations.
acceptance: For a sequential diagram over one A, the same index m works at every stage and yields the bound 2m on the colimit.
For A=𝔽_p[x₁,x₂,…]/(x₁²,x₂³,…) and I=(x₁,x₂,…), every finite-generator subideal is nilpotent, but I is not nilpotent and A→A/I is not descendable. This detects removal of the uniform bound.
Identity maps have index at most 1; zero source unit allows index 0, so no convention silently excludes the degenerate case.

sources.match: Proves the sequential uniform-index bound and records nilpotent, Gorenstein and countability applications; the general finite-cohomological-dimension filtration input remains explicit.

nodes.title: Formal inversion of a tensor object
nodes.statement: For presentably symmetric monoidal C and X∈C, C[X⁻¹] is initial among presentably symmetric monoidal categories receiving a colimit-preserving strong monoidal functor from C in which X becomes tensor invertible. For a presentable C-module M its base change M⊗_C C[X⁻¹] is the universal inversion of X on M. If the cyclic permutation of X⊗X⊗X is homotopic to the identity, its underlying presentable category is the colimit in PrL of the telescope M→M→⋯ with transition X⊗−. Without this symmetric-object hypothesis the telescope formula is not asserted.
hypotheses: Universes and presentability are fixed.
The cyclic symmetry is a coherent homotopy condition, not equality in an ordinary Grothendieck group.
proofSteps: Construct the inversion as a localization in commutative algebra objects of PrL.
Base change modules along its universal map.
Apply Robalo’s symmetric-object argument to identify the telescope, checking the permutation hypothesis.
acceptance: Inverting the unit changes C by an equivalence.
Inverting zero in a stable C gives the zero category.
Inverting the already inverted object again changes nothing.

nodes.title: Compact objects
nodes.statement: For regular κ, an object x of C is κ-compact if Map_C(x,−) preserves κ-filtered colimits. Compact means ω-compact. Write C^κ for the full subcategory. In a presentable stable C, compact generation means a small set of compact objects whose shifts detect zero. Finite colimits and retracts of compact objects are compact. Compactness is a mapping-space condition, not merely finite generation of the cohomology groups.

nodes.statement: Ind_κ(C) is the full subcategory of P(C)=Fun(Cop,Spaces) spanned by κ-filtered colimits of representables. nodes.title: The universal property of Ind
nodes.statement: For small C and D admitting κ-filtered colimits, restriction along Yoneda gives Fun_κ(Ind_κ(C),D) ≃ Fun(C,D). The extension sends a filtered presentation colim_i y(c_i) to colim_i F(c_i), independently of the presentation. For κ=ω, if C has finite colimits, D is presentable and F preserves finite colimits, its Ind extension preserves all small colimits. For larger κ, the corresponding criterion requires κ-small colimits and their preservation, rather than finite colimits alone. The extension is an equivalence exactly when the input is fully faithful, its objects are κ-compact in D, and they κ-filtered-generate D.
hypotheses: The equivalence criterion refers to the stated fully faithful input, not an arbitrary functor.
proofSteps: Apply the E3 full-inclusion left Kan extension to Yoneda.
Use filtered presentations to prove evaluation and uniqueness on mapping spaces.
Use compactness to prove full faithfulness of the extension, then generation for essential surjectivity.

For ω, use the finite-colimit completion property and filtered-colimit preservation to obtain all colimits. In the presentable κ-accessible case apply HTT 5.5.1.9 with κ-small colimits of compact objects; do not substitute finite colimits at larger κ.
acceptance: Restriction of the extension of F is naturally equivalent to F; two filtered presentations of one Ind-object give the same mapping-space comparison.

nodes.title: Stable and monoidal Ind-completion
nodes.statement: For small stable C, Ind_κ(C) is stable and Yoneda is exact. For small symmetric monoidal C, Ind(C) has a symmetric monoidal structure whose tensor preserves filtered colimits separately and extends C’s tensor. If C is stable and tensor exact separately, this tensor preserves all colimits separately. Exact strong monoidal functors on C extend to colimit-preserving strong monoidal functors on Ind(C); uniqueness includes their coherent monoidal structure.
hypotheses: The monoidal colimit-preservation conclusion needs stability and exactness, not just existence of tensor.
proofSteps: Express arrows as filtered colimits of arrows in C and compute their cofibers.
Use finite-limit commutation with filtered colimits in spaces to identify fibers.
Apply the monoidal free-colimit completion in HA 4.8.1.14; check finite cofiber compatibility to upgrade filtered preservation to all colimits.
acceptance: The Ind Yoneda functor preserves the zero object, cofibers and the E0 suspension convention.
Tensor of two filtered representable presentations is computed by the product filtered diagram, and the unit is the representable original unit.

nodes.title: Presentable infinity-categories
nodes.statement: C is presentable when it is accessible and admits all small colimits. Equivalently it is an accessible reflective localization of a presheaf infinity-category. PrL has these objects and colimit-preserving functors; PrR uses accessible right adjoints. Accessibility entails a regular cardinal and an essentially small subcategory of compact objects generating by that cardinal’s filtered colimits. Presentability alone does not assert compact generation at ω.
hypotheses: Maintain the specified universe of small colimits.
Representability and adjoint existence are supplied by E3, including the accessibility condition.
proofSteps: Describe accessibility by the essentially small κ-compact subcategory and its filtered generation.
Construct the space-valued presheaf category using E0 functor/limit infrastructure; use HTT 5.5.1.1 to compare accessible presheaf localizations with the definition.
Define PrL and PrR by their coherent preservation/adjoint properties; E1’s concrete sheaf application imports this generic definition.

The zero stable category is presentable.

nodes.title: Limits in PrL
nodes.statement: Every small diagram of presentable categories and colimit-preserving functors has a limit in PrL, and its underlying category is the limit in Cat∞. Colimits in that limit are detected and computed by the projections. In particular pullbacks of presentable colimit-preserving functors are presentable. The limit remains stable when the diagram categories are stable. This does not imply that an unrelated forgetful functor from a completed subcategory preserves colimits.
hypotheses: The diagram is coherent in PrL, not a diagram of triangulated categories.
proofSteps: Construct the Cat∞ limit using E0/E3 coherent diagrams.
Use the presentable pullback theorem and accessible-localization presentations to verify presentability.

acceptance: The limit of a diagram over one point is its input; the empty limit is the terminal presentable category.
In a pullback C×_E D of left adjoints, projections compute coproducts and cofibers componentwise.
A completed-module inclusion into ambient modules can fail to preserve coproducts; this does not contradict the theorem, since that inclusion need not be a PrL map.

Its right adjoint is fully faithful and preserves colimits; the right adjoint extends the quotient-Yoneda approximation C/D→Ind(C). nodes.title: Compactness and right adjoints
nodes.statement: For F:C⇄D:G between presentable stable categories, if C is compactly generated then F preserves compact objects if and only if G preserves coproducts, equivalently all colimits. The forward direction tests the coproduct comparison against compact generators of C; the reverse uses the mapping-space adjunction. The general κ-accessible version replaces compact/coproduct preservation by κ-compact/κ-filtered preservation with the accessibility hypotheses of HTT 5.5.7.2.

G is already exact as a right adjoint between stable categories.
proofSteps: Apply the adjunction to maps out of compact source generators.

Use exactness plus coproduct preservation to obtain all colimits, and the adjunction to get preservation of compactness back.

nodes.title: Coherent actions and continuous fixed points
nodes.statement: For a finite group G, an action on C is a coherent functor BG→Cat∞, equivalently a cocartesian fibration over BG. Its homotopy fixed point category is its limit; for two actions, equivariant functors are the homotopy fixed points of Fun(C,D) under conjugation. Presentable stable actions by equivalences have presentable stable fixed point categories. For a profinite G, categorical actions factoring through a specified finite quotient are pulled back coherently from that quotient. The continuous coefficient specialization uses the E1 enhancement of discrete continuous G-modules: derived invariants agree with the canonical continuous-cochain object and, in degree n, the ProfiniteCohomology finite-quotient system colim_U Hⁿ(G/U,M^U). No filtered-colimit formula for arbitrary categorical homotopy fixed points is asserted.
hypotheses: For profinite coefficient modules M the topology is discrete and stabilizers of each element are open.
The all-degree finite-quotient statement is ProfiniteCohomology Layer 10; Layer 4 supplies only degrees 0,1,2.
General topological actions on Cat∞ beyond finite-quotient factoring require a chosen continuity model.
proofSteps: Use the arbitrary-base extension of E0 straightening and coherent limits to construct actions and fixed points.
Construct conjugation coherently on the functor category and take its limit.
For continuous modules use E1’s enhancement and import the existing ProfiniteCohomology dictionary and canonical comparisons; do not replan its cochain theory.
acceptance: The trivial group has C as its fixed point category.
The trivial action of finite G on C has fixed point category Fun(BG,C).
For finite G and coefficients M, derived invariants agree with ordinary group cohomology in every nonnegative degree.

nodes.title: Compact morphisms and compact exhaustions

nodes.title: Dualizable and compactly assembled categories
nodes.statement: A presentable stable C is dualizable in PrL_st if it admits a dual, evaluation and coevaluation with triangle homotopies. nodes.title: Filtered colimits of dualizable categories
nodes.statement: A left adjoint is strongly continuous when its right adjoint also preserves colimits. A filtered diagram of dualizable stable presentable categories with strongly continuous transitions has dualizable colimit in PrL_st. The canonical comparison from the colimit of their compact subcategories to the compact subcategory of the result is an equivalence, with colimits of small stable categories taken in the idempotent-complete convention. nodes.title: Trace-class maps and rigid categories
nodes.statement: In a presentable closed symmetric monoidal C, f:x→y is trace-class if there are d, a pairing d⊗x→1 and a map 1→y⊗d whose contraction is f. Equivalently its class in Hom(x,y) lifts through Hom(x,1)⊗y. C is locally rigid over V when it is dualizable as a V-module and multiplication C⊗_V C→C is an internal left adjoint over C⊗_V C: its right adjoint preserves colimits and is bilinear. It is rigid when additionally its unit is V-atomic; absolutely over Sp this means compact. In the absolute stable case local rigidity is equivalent to dualizability plus every compact morphism being trace-class. Compact unit together with trace-class compact exhaustions generating under colimits implies rigidity.
hypotheses: Objectwise dualizability is distinct from categorical rigidity.
Absolute stable formulations use the abstract unit Sp of PrL_st, not a concrete spectrum model.

Use the internal adjoint criterion for multiplication, with both linearity and preservation of colimits.

nodes.title: Frobenius discreteness and perfection
nodes.statement: For a simplicial commutative 𝔽_p-algebra A, Frobenius acts by zero on π_i(A) for i>0. Thus perfection, the sequential Frobenius colimit, is discrete and equals the perfection of π₀A. Perfect discrete 𝔽_p-algebras are closed under ordinary and derived colimits. In particular a derived tensor of perfect B←A→C is discrete, perfect and equals its ordinary tensor. The perfection of a derived affine scheme is the perfection of its classical truncation; global scheme glueing is imported from E1/E2. The multiplication map A×A→A, based at (0,0), induces zero on positive homotopy because its restrictions to both axes are zero. This does not say multiplication as a bilinear graded ring operation vanishes. An imperfect base cannot be dropped: for A=𝔽_p(t), A_perf⊗_A A_perf has the nonzero nilpotent t^(1/p)⊗1−1⊗t^(1/p). Cosimplicial perfection need not be discrete, as the perfected elliptic-cohomology example in Remark 11.7 shows.
hypotheses: p is prime and the algebra is commutative simplicial in characteristic p.
A cosimplicial or arbitrary E∞ algebra does not satisfy this assertion.
proofSteps: Resolve A by free simplicial algebras and calculate Frobenius on positive homotopy using the graded free resolution argument in BS.
Use filtered-colimit preservation of π_i to kill all positive homotopy in perfection.
Apply the same calculation to derived pushouts between perfect rings; identify π₀ with the ordinary pushout.
acceptance: For A=𝔽_p⊗ᴸ_{𝔽_p[x]}𝔽_p, π₁A=𝔽_p while its perfection is discrete; the theorem must kill this genuine derived class.
For perfect B←A→C with perfect A, all positive Tor groups vanish.
Over the imperfect base 𝔽_p(t), the ordinary tensor of two perfections has the displayed nonzero nilpotent; perfect endpoints alone do not imply a perfect pushout.

nodes.title: The simplicial Witt adapter
nodes.statement: Apply the existing p-typical Witt vector functor degreewise to a simplicial commutative 𝔽_p-algebra A. This preserves weak equivalences since its underlying simplicial set is A^ℕ, with π_i W(A)≅∏_ℕ π_i A as pointed homotopy sets. For i>0 this is an additive-group identification by Eckmann–Hilton; at i=0 the ring is W(π₀A), whose addition is the Witt addition rather than coordinatewise addition. Witt Frobenius induces zero on positive homotopy; its sequential localization is discrete and the map to W(π₀A) becomes an equivalence after Frobenius localization. The fibre of W(A)→W(π₀A) is killed by p in the derived sense, using the coherent Witt identity VF=p and the Frobenius nullhomotopy, rather than inferring a null map just from p-torsion cohomology.

nodes.title: Bounded totalizations and filtered colimits
nodes.statement: For a cosimplicial diagram of n-truncated spaces, n≥0 fixed, totalization equals partial totalization through degree n+1. Consequently totalization commutes with filtered colimits when the truncation bound is uniform in both indices. For cosimplicial spectra whose terms all lie in Sp≤b for one integer b, π_k of totalization is computed by a finite partial stage r≥max(0,b−k+1). This gives filtered-colimit commutation degree by degree; coconnective terms are the case b=0. The analogous cohomological comparison for complexes uses a uniform lower cohomological bound. Without a uniform bound, arbitrary totalization need not commute with filtered colimits. Unbounded Postnikov convergence and hypercompleteness are supplied by E2.
hypotheses: The bound must hold uniformly over both the filtered index and cosimplicial degree.
A claim that an arbitrary infinite limit commutes with filtered colimits is excluded.
proofSteps: Use the Reedy matching-object tower: extending Tot_(r−1) to Tot_r has obstruction in degree r−1 of the matching fibre and space of lifts Ωʳ of that fibre. For n-truncated spaces, obstructions and choices vanish for r>n+1, so Tot_(n+1) determines the result.
For spectra bounded above by b, the layer Ωʳ of a matching fibre is bounded above by b−r. Both π_k and π_(k−1) of that layer vanish for r>b−k+1, giving the displayed stable-degree window.

Partial totalizations are finite iterated homotopy limits built from matching diagrams. Filtered colimits commute with these finite limits and with homotopy groups, giving the comparison; E2 supplies convergence when using a more general Postnikov reconstruction.
acceptance: For 0-truncated terms, Tot₁ is the equalizer condition and suffices. For 1-truncated terms, Tot₂ must also impose coherence.
The same truncation bound is used for every filtered input, and the comparison uses finite homotopy limits rather than an infinite product interchange.
For spectra in Sp≤0, each π_k uses the window r≥max(0,1−k); the argument supplies no single finite stage for the whole spectrum.

sources.locator: §11, footnote 23, p. 46; the coconnective-spectra argument in the proof of Proposition 11.41, p. 53
sources.match: Uses uniform n-truncation for space-valued totalizations and coconnectivity for spectral totalizations. The finite-stage bounds above are obtained from the matching-fibre obstruction tower; no unbounded commutation theorem is attributed to this source.
